Two inconsistencies would break code that uses `REGISTRY` / `get()`. The worst is **`shop/carriers/maple.py`**.

**1. `maple.py` takes weight in grams; every other carrier takes kilograms.** The 19 other modules say "weight in kg" and use `PER_KG` / `MAX_KG`. Maple says "weight in grams" and uses `PER_GRAMS = 3` and `MAX_GRAMS = 30000` (`maple.py:2`, `:8`, `:10`, `:17`, `:20`). The method signature is the same, `rate(self, weight: float, zone="local")`, so nothing fails visibly. A caller passing kg to every carrier through the registry gets this:
- `get("maple").rate(5)` is read as 5 g and returns about 509 cents. A 5 kg parcel should cost about 15,494 cents, so Maple is roughly 30× too cheap and will win any cheapest-carrier comparison.
- Its weight limit is effectively 30,000 kg instead of 30 kg, so overweight parcels are accepted when they should raise `ValueError`.

**2. Four carriers don't have `tracking_url()`: `delta.py`, `kestrel.py`, `onyx.py` and `tundra.py`.** The other 16 define it. Calling `get(name).tracking_url(code)` on any of these four raises `AttributeError`. Each one stops right after `valid_label()`.

I found nothing else. I compared every module's structure against `acme.py` with carrier names and numbers masked. The other differences are only per-carrier rates, zone factors, weight limits and label prefixes. Every module has the same three zone keys (`local`, `regional`, `national`), and every class has `name` and the same method signatures.

I didn't find any code outside `shop/carriers/` that calls the registry yet, so nothing in the repo is broken today. These would hit the first caller that treats the carriers as interchangeable. I didn't edit any files.
